items.question: When is the best time to take a Galápagos cruise?
items.answer: The Galápagos is a year-round destination. The warm season (December–May) brings calmer seas and clearer water for snorkeling, while the cool, dry season (June–November) is best for seabirds and marine wildlife. Departures run every week: browse the full fleet to compare open dates.

items.question: How many days do I need for a Galápagos cruise?
items.answer: Most itineraries run 4, 5 or 8 days. Shorter cruises focus on the central islands; longer ones reach the more remote western and northern islands. Each ship runs set routes (A/B/C): check the day-by-day itinerary on any ship page.

items.question: What is the difference between the cruise classes?
items.answer: We group ships into three classes by comfort and service level: Luxury, First Class and Tourist Superior. All follow the same national-park routes with naturalist guides; the difference is cabin size, cuisine and onboard amenities.

items.question: Which islands and wildlife will I see?
items.answer: The exact islands depend on the ship's itinerary. Expect giant tortoises, marine iguanas, sea lions, blue-footed boobies and, depending on the route, penguins, flamingos or waved albatross. The itinerary section on each ship page lists the sites visited day by day.

items.question: Is a Galápagos cruise suitable for families or older travellers?
items.answer: Yes. Activity levels vary by ship and itinerary: some routes involve longer hikes and panga (dinghy) rides, others are gentler. Tell us who's travelling and we'll match you to the right ship. Ask for a recommendation.

items.question: Do I need to know how to swim or scuba dive?
items.answer: No. Snorkeling is optional and gear is provided, and most ships offer stable panga rides for those who prefer to stay dry. If you specifically want diving, filter the fleet for Scuba Diving liveaboards.

items.question: What should I pack for a Galápagos cruise?
items.answer: Lightweight, quick-dry clothing, a hat, reef-safe sunscreen, a light rain jacket, sturdy walking shoes and a swimsuit. Snorkel gear is usually provided on board. Pack light, since cabins and internal flight baggage allowances are limited.

items.question: How far in advance should I book?
items.answer: Popular ships and holiday dates sell out months ahead, so book as early as you can for the widest choice of cabins and departures. Live availability on each ship page shows what's currently open: request a quote to hold a space.
